title: Ice Cream 1.5L

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Same price in 2026-09-28 led to 24 units (x0.54 vs baseline); suggests demand drop under price rise.

drivers.name: Supply delivery short
drivers.evidence: Planner note warns of short delivery; likely reduces available stock and customer intent.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 44.6. Halloween (event week) has a noise-adjusted multiplier of x1.0, so no uplift. The price increase to $6.56 (+2.3%) is modest and not likely to drive demand. However, the recent week (2026-09-28) at the same price saw a dip to 24 units (x0.54 vs baseline), suggesting price sensitivity. The planner note of a short delivery implies supply risk, which may suppress demand. The past promotion uplifts (x1.25 noise-adjusted) are relevant, but no promotion is scheduled. The prior week after a promotion typically sees 0.83x, but no prior promotion occurred. No strong driver justifies a move from 1.0. Confidence is medium due to thin evidence on price and supply impact.

brief:
PRODUCT: Ice Cream 1.5L | category Frozen | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01 (3 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Holiday: Halloween (Sat)
  shelf price: 6.56 (+2.3% vs regular price 6.41)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 44.6 | 5%-95%: 17.1 - 70.6 | 10%-90%: 24.4 - 66.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-36% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
